story.head: A long night for Joey Daccord
paras: The Kraken (10-9-1) lost 4-3 to San Jose on Saturday, and the Ducks are on a three-game losing streak. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Ducks fourth (22nd in the NHL) and the Kraken sixth (24th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
The Ducks’ record (.479) is about what their chances are worth. The Kraken’s record (.525) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.439), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Ducks hit a lot (5th), give up a lot of dangerous shots (31st) and have had shaky goaltending (30th). The Kraken, by contrast, keep dangerous shots away (1st). Anaheim has allowed 3.83 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. The Kraken rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd). They also give up a lot of shots (32nd), so the Ducks are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against them. Both teams like to play fast, so expect an open game.

Cutter Gauthier (21 G / 9 A / 30 P in 23 GP) leads the Ducks in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Mikael Granlund (8 G / 18 A / 26 P in 23 GP) is next in line. For the Kraken, Berkly Catton (8 G / 10 A / 18 P in 20 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Brandon Montour (3 G / 12 A / 15 P in 19 GP) is next in line.
Lukáš Dostál (4-6-1 / .857 SV% in 12 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Anaheim, but is expected to start. Joey Daccord (4-4-0 / .872 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to go for Seattle.
